feedback: Encourage both a seen cue and a felt cue for each weather word (e.g. sunny: 'the sun is shining and there are shadows' and 'I can feel the sun on my skin', even if the air is cold).
If a child only describes the picture, prompt 'what would it feel like outside?' to bring in touch and sound.
activities.intendedInsight: Weather is experienced through more than one sense — it is felt and heard as well as seen — which enriches the descriptive vocabulary.
learnerActions: Look at each weather image and pair it with a sense-word: sunny–bright (you may feel the sun on your skin, even on a cold day), snowy–cold, rainy–wet, windy–blowy.
Describe both what you can see and what it would feel like on your skin for today's weather.
Use sound and touch descriptions (the whoosh of wind, the patter of rain) to add to the weather word.
activities.title: Sensory pairing: weather you feel as well as see

feedback: For a correct match, restate the cue that justified it ('yes — grey cloud all over, so cloudy').
For the grey-sky scene, if a child says 'no weather', widen the category: cloudy, windy and foggy are all weather; ask what the sky and air are doing, not just what is falling.
activities.intendedInsight: Confirm that the weather words and symbols have stuck and can be applied to real conditions.
learnerActions: Match each photo of real weather to the correct word and its symbol, going both ways (photo→word and symbol→word).
Choose which word best describes a shown scene (e.g. a grey overcast sky with nothing falling → 'cloudy').
Say what today's weather is in a full short sentence using the shared words.
activities.title: Match and describe: check the vocabulary

feedback: Gently extend a child's everyday word toward the shared science word (e.g. 'chucking it down' → 'rainy, really heavy rain').
If a child names only the temperature, ask separately what the sky is doing to pull weather and temperature apart.
activities.intendedInsight: Children can produce weather descriptions in their own words, not just recognise them.
learnerActions: Pretend to be a weather reporter and tell a friendly presenter what the weather is like today.
Answer 'how can you tell?' by naming a cue you can see or feel.
Extend your own words when the presenter offers the matching shared weather word.
activities.title: Weather-reporter chat: say what it's like out there (optional)
